sections.title: A spiny dryland fruit tree
sections.text: Indian jujube is a thorny shrub or small tree of seasonally dry tropical regions, commonly 3–15 m tall. Its branches carry alternate oval leaves with three prominent veins and small greenish-yellow flowers. The image's tree, leaves, flowers and reddish oval drupes are consistent with the species.

sections.title: Fruit and seed
sections.text: The edible drupe varies among varieties, ripening from green to yellow, orange or red-brown; flesh may be crisp and sour-sweet or become mealy when fully ripe. Reports give fruit lengths from about 1.8 to 5 cm, reflecting cultivar variation. Each fruit contains a hard stone; the fruit flesh is eaten fresh, dried or preserved. The sources do not recommend eating the stone or seeds.
